newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain firms say parties keen on labour reform deal.
newsitem.headline: Spain firms say parties keen on labour reform deal.

text.p: Spanish unions and businessmen clearly intend to reach an agreement on the reform of the labour market, secretary general of employers' association CEOE Juan Jimenez Aguilar said on Wednesday.
"There is clearly a will to find points of agreement both from the unions and from our point of view," Jimenez said at a two-day Herald Tribune conference.
On Tuesday, Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar urged parties to reach a basic agreement on labour reform.
CEOE's Jimenez said Spain needed to overcome the current division between temporary and permanent jobs.
"We have a divided workforce...with the privileges of the ins and the problems of the outs," he said.
Employers would like to reform the labour market to make it more stable by removing the division and giving firms more certainty on firing policy and lowering costs of dismissal.
Since 1994, when the previous Socialist government approved a jobs market reform that enhanced the use of temporary contracts, these types of agreements have become widespread in Spain.
The 1994 reform had not set up an appropriate "hire and fire policy," Jimenez said.
